title: What a Probability Is
objective: After this level you can place a chance on the scale from impossible (0) to certain (1) and explain it as a long-run share of outcomes.
summary: A probability is a number from 0 (never) to 1 (always). It describes the long run, the share of times something happens over many tries, and for equally likely outcomes you count and divide.

cards.headline: A coin has a 1 in 2 chance of heads. So what will the next flip be?
cards.body: Nobody knows, and nobody can. A probability doesn't predict one flip. It tells you something sturdier, about what happens when you flip again and again. This level shows what that number really measures.

cards.headline: Every chance lives between 0 and 1
cards.body: Probabilities run on a scale from 0 to 1. A 0 means the event never happens, like rolling a 7 on one ordinary die, whose faces only go from 1 to 6. A 1 means it always happens. Halfway, 0.5 means it's as likely to happen as not. Chapter 1's tools still work here: 0.5 is 50%, or 1 in 2. The closer to 1, the likelier the event.

cards.headline: A probability is a long-run share
cards.body: So what does 0.5 promise for a coin? Not the next flip. It describes the long run: flip a fair coin 20 times, then 2,000, then 20,000, and the share of heads creeps closer and closer to 0.5. That's how statisticians define it: the probability of an outcome is its long-term relative frequency. One flip is a surprise. Twenty thousand flips are a pattern.

cards.fact: When outcomes are equally likely, count them.
cards.context: A fair die's six faces are equally likely. What's the chance of rolling at least 5? Two faces (5 and 6) out of six, so 2 in 6, which is 1 in 3. Count the outcomes you want, divide by all the outcomes, and you have a probability. That simple rule powers the next few levels.

cards.headline: Probability: defined
learned: A probability is a long-run share

questions.prompt: Match each probability with what it means.

pairs.right: As likely to happen as not

questions.explanation: A probability of 0 means the event never happens, 1 means it always happens, and 0.5 means it's as likely to happen as not.

questions.prompt: How does a 0.5 chance of heads actually show up when you flip a fair coin?

options.label: Every second flip lands heads
options.rationale: Flips follow no set pattern; only the long-run share is predictable.

options.label: Exactly 10 heads in every 20 flips
options.rationale: Twenty flips can easily give 8 or 12 heads.

options.label: Heads and tails take turns
options.rationale: Coins don't alternate; the share settles only over many flips.

options.label: The share of heads nears half over many flips

questions.explanation: A probability is a long-run share: over 20, 2,000 and 20,000 flips, the share of heads gets closer and closer to 0.5.

questions.prompt: Written as "1 in N" (Level 7), the chance of rolling at least 5 on a fair die is _____.

options.label: 1 in 2
options.rationale: That would need three of the six faces.

options.label: 1 in 5
options.rationale: The die has six faces, not five; count 2 out of 6.

options.label: 1 in 6
options.rationale: That is the chance of one face; at least 5 covers two.

questions.explanation: Two faces (5 and 6) out of six equally likely faces: 2 in 6, which is 1 in 3.
